note: Time Formatter provides one field formatter plugin, number_time ('Time'), for integer/decimal/float fields. It interprets the numeric value as seconds or milliseconds and renders a time string. Settings (config schema field.formatter.settings.number_time): storage (0=Seconds,1=Milliseconds; default 1), display (0='123h 59m 59s 999ms',1='123h 59m 59s',2='123:59:59.999',3='123:59:59'; default 2), hours (0=Always,1=Optional,2=Never; default 0). No settings page, permission, drush, or plugin type. Cases are grounded in that real formatter config on an entity_view_display: introspection reads back the formatter/settings on a live field display; execution applies the number_time formatter to a field and changes its settings, verified against the live view display config.

evals.prompt: I have an integer field on a Drupal 11 site that stores a duration. Which formatter does the time_formatter module add to display it as a time, and which field types can use it?
evals.expected_output: The 'Time' formatter (plugin id number_time), available on integer, decimal and float fields. Set it as the field's format on Manage display to render the number as a time string.

evals.prompt: What settings does the time_formatter 'Time' (number_time) formatter offer, and what does the storage setting mean?
evals.expected_output: Three settings: storage (Seconds vs Milliseconds - how to interpret the stored number, default Milliseconds), display (the output format, e.g. 123h 59m 59s 999ms / 123:59:59.999 / 123:59:59), and hours (Always / Optional / Never).

evals.prompt: Which display formats can the time_formatter number_time formatter produce, and which of its formats include milliseconds?
evals.expected_output: Four display options: '123h 59m 59s 999ms' (0) and '123:59:59.999' (2) include milliseconds; '123h 59m 59s' (1) and '123:59:59' (3) drop them. Default is '123:59:59.999'.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article field field_tf_probe is displayed with the time_formatter module. Inspect the live default view display and state which formatter plugin id is configured for that field.
evals.expected_output: The formatter is number_time ('Time'), from core.entity_view_display.node.article.default -> content.field_tf_probe.type (settings storage=0/Seconds, display=3).

evals.prompt: The Article field field_tf_probe on this site uses the time_formatter 'Time' formatter. Inspect the live view-display configuration and state whether its value is interpreted as seconds or milliseconds (the storage setting).
evals.expected_output: It is interpreted as Seconds: the number_time formatter's storage setting is 0 (Seconds) on field_tf_probe's default view-display component.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the Article integer field field_tf_task currently displays as a plain number. Using time_formatter, change its default display so it uses the 'Time' formatter and interprets the stored value as seconds. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: In core.entity_view_display.node.article.default the field_tf_task component has type number_time with settings.storage = 0 (Seconds).

evals.prompt: The Article field field_tf_switch on this site already uses the time_formatter 'Time' formatter but always shows an hours component. Reconfigure it so the hours component is never shown (Hours: Never), keeping the Time formatter. Apply the change live.
evals.expected_output: field_tf_switch keeps type number_time and its settings.hours becomes 2 (Never) in core.entity_view_display.node.article.default.
